'''Renaud Lambiotte''' is a Belgian mathematician and physicist who is currently the Professor of Networks and Nonlinear Systems at the [[Mathematical Institute]], [[University of Oxford]], and a tutorial fellow at [[Somerville College]], University of Oxford.<ref name="Oxford">{{cite web | title=Renaud Lambiotte &#124; Mathematical Institute | url=https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/people/renaud.lambiotte }}</ref> He has contributed to the field of [[complex networks]]. He became a fellow of the  [[Fellows of the Network Science Society|Network Science Society]] in 2025.<ref name="NetSci">{{cite web | title=NetSci – the Network Science Society | url=https://netscisociety.net/award-prizes/society-fellows }}</ref>

== Career ==

Born in [[Namur]], [[Belgium]], Lambiotte went on to study physics at [[Université libre de Bruxelles]], graduating with a Master's degree.<ref name="SIAM">{{cite web | title=Professional Feature - Renaud Lambiotte | url=https://dsweb.siam.org/The-Magazine/Article/professional-feature-renaud-lambiotte }}</ref> He completed his [[PhD]] in 2004 with a thesis entitled ''Inelastic Gases: A Paradigm for Far-from-equilibrium Systems'', supervised by [[Léon Brenig]].<ref name="MathGene">{{cite web | title=Renaud Lambiotte - the Mathematics Genealogy Project | url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=140104 }}</ref> Following this, Lambiotte completed [[post-docs]] at [[ENS Lyon]], the [[University of Liège]], [[UC Louvain]], and [[Imperial College London]] where he pivoted to the study of complex networks.<ref name="Oxford" /><ref name="SIAM" /><ref name="Personal">{{Cite web |title=Renaud Lambiotte |url=https://www.lambiotte.be/ |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=www.lambiotte.be}}</ref> In 2011, he joined the faculty at the Department of Mathematics at the [[University of Namur]] and the [[Namur Institute For Complex Systems]] as an [[Assistant Professor]], becoming [[Professor]] in 2014. In 2017, he moved to the Mathematical Institute at the University of Oxford as an [[Associate Professor]], becoming Professor in 2020.<ref name="Oxford" />

In 2015, he shared the Verdickt-Rijdams Prize from the [[Académie royale de langue et de littérature françaises de Belgique]] for ''La tortue de Zénon'', a book collection on the relations between science and literature.<ref>{{cite web | title=Prix Verdickt-Rijdams 2015: Les éditions l'Arbre de Diane pour la collection «La tortue de Zénon» | url=https://www.arllfb.be/prixlitteraires/prixverdicktrijdams/2015.html }}</ref>

== Research ==
Lambiotte has made contributions to both theoretical and applied topics in network science. His research has focused on [[network dynamics]] with applications to [[Large-scale brain network|brain networks]] and [[social networks]].<ref name="Oxford" /> He is a co-author of the books ''A Guide to Temporal Networks'' with [[Naoki Masuda]]<ref>Masuda, Naoki and Lambiotte, Renaud (2016). ''A Guide to Temporal Networks''. World Scientific Publishing. ISBN 9781786341167.</ref> and ''Modularity and Dynamics on Complex Networks'' with [[Michael Schaub]].<ref>Lambiotte, Renaud and Schaub, Michael (2021). ''Modularity and Dynamics on Complex Networks''. Cambridge University Press. ISBN 9781108774116.</ref>

=== Community detection ===

Lambiotte has made contributions to the problem of [[community structure|community detection]] in complex networks. Whilst at UCLouvain, he was a co-author of the [[Louvain method]],<ref>{{Cite journal

 | first1 = Vincent D.
 | last2 = Guillaume
 | first2 = Jean-Loup
 | last3 = Lambiotte
 | first3 = Renaud
 | last4 = Lefebvre
 | first4 = Etienne
 | title = Fast unfolding of communities in large networks
 | journal = Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment
 | year = 2008
 | issue = 10
 | article-number = P10008
 | doi = 10.1088/1742-5468/2008/10/P10008
| arxiv = 0803.0476
 | bibcode = 2008JSMTE..10..008B
 }}</ref> an algorithm for maximising [[modularity]], which has gone on to be to cited more than 20,000 times.<ref>{{Cite journal
 | last1 = Blondel
 | first1 = Vincent D.
 | last2 = Guillaume
 | first2 = Jean-Loup
 | last3 = Lambiotte
 | first3 = Renaud
 | title = Fast unfolding of communities in large networks: 15 years later
 | journal = Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment
 | year = 2024
| issue = 10
 | pages = 10R001
 | doi = 10.1088/1742-5468/ad6139
 | arxiv = 2311.06047
 | bibcode = 2024JSMTE2024jR001B
 }}</ref>
